scenarios.title: The Boomer Bastion
scenarios.briefing: It is day one of WW3. Several NATO assets have been held back from other combat duties with the specific purpose of attacking the Soviet boomers at home in their bastion. Additionally, the SOSUS line must be manned to protect a passing convoy.
scenarios.victoryConditions: NATO wins the game by sinking an SSBN payload value of 9. The Soviet player may reduce the current Payload value back by one for each Soviet submarine step that makes it over the SOSUS line (remove it from the game). The minimum resting total is zero (it cannot be negative). NATO may add one Payload value point work by damaging or sinking the Kiev.
scenarios.specialRules: The Bastion cannot have Bad Weather (ignore any such results) but otherwise generate weather for East and North. No cards are used in this scenario. Optionally, both players can draw five cards at the start of the game and use only Reaction Events — ignore the rest of the card.
scenarios.opsTrackNote: Uses the small-scenario 1-5 OPS Track (records cycle through boxes 1-5 instead of the full 1-10 track).

alterations.title: Scenario 1a: Yankee Hunting
alterations.description:
Setup as Scenario #1, then layer the Yankee SSBN hunt on top:

- One Yankee step must be killed for NATO to win the game.
- NATO may add a Payload value point at the end of each turn if any Yankee is more than 1 zone from a First Strike zone.
- The Soviet units starting the game over the SOSUS line cannot reduce the current Payload value sunk by crossing over the SOSUS line — the scenario special rule is ignored for them.
- NATO OPS increase to 7.
- Generate weather for Mid and West zones as well (everything except the Mediterranean).

notes: **Needs review (uncorroborated handwritten note):** Marginal handwriting on page 2 of the scenario book reads 'Boomers cannot return to port; must stay at sea.' This restriction is not found in the 2020 errata rulebook, v1.17 rulebook, or designer Q&A. Matt to confirm whether this is a house rule, scenario-specific intent, or a misread.

scenarios.title: Ace Mobile & First Convoys
scenarios.briefing: D+2. While the fight rages underwater in the North, NATO sorties convoys to sea heading for the French ports. Meanwhile ACE Mobile — NATO's rapid reaction force — sets off from the UK to Trondheim. The Soviets have earmarked two regiments of naval aviation and 18 submarines to interdict these forces.
scenarios.victoryConditions: When a Convoy/Amphib reaches port remove the entire Task Force from the scenario. The Soviets must interdict; NATO must deliver.
scenarios.specialRules: Prior to beginning play NATO may move any two Air Units and put them On Patrol. The British may deploy their Surface Units in up to 2 different Task Forces as desired, beginning in British ports but formed up so there is no further OPS cost to sail them. The Soviet player has one spy available; after every use remove it from the game on a roll of 1-4. UK Air Units cannot enter the North 9-10 zone in this scenario. No cards are used in this scenario. Optionally, both players can draw five cards at the start of the game and use only Reaction Events — ignore the rest of the card.

alterations.title: Scenario 2a: Extended
alterations.description:
Setup as Scenario #2 with these changes:

- The Soviets must hit all three targets (Convoys & Amphib) for three hits apiece, OR six hits on any two, to win the game.
- Soviet OPS increase to 9 per turn.

scenarios.title: Kirov's & Carriers
scenarios.briefing: The NATO carrier battle groups clash with the bulk of the Soviet surface fleet in the Norwegian Sea, with both sides racing to seize the initiative around Trondheim.
scenarios.victoryConditions: NATO must execute the Amphibious Landing at Trondheim while protecting the US carrier groups. Soviet wins by sinking carrier value before the landing succeeds.
scenarios.specialRules: Amphibious Landing at Trondheim is the NATO objective. Soviet surface fleet operates at full strength from Kola and Baltic bases.

alterations.title: The Days Before
alterations.description: Start with the Soviet ships all in port, and the US carrier Task Forces both 2 zones West of their parallel-at-start positions. This allows the fight to develop, rather than being a knife fight in a phone booth.

scenarios.title: Attack on the Kola Peninsula
scenarios.briefing: NATO strikes directly at the Soviet Northern Fleet's home base in the Kola Peninsula. Carrier-based strikes face the full weight of Soviet land-based naval aviation and SAM defenses.
scenarios.victoryConditions: NATO wins by inflicting sufficient hits on Kola facilities and Soviet capital ships. Soviet wins by sinking NATO carriers / breaking the strike before objectives are met.
scenarios.specialRules: The scenario lasts a maximum of 5 turns. Soviet naval air operates at full strength from Kola bases.

alterations.title: #1 Use Nuclear Weapons
alterations.description: Try the scenario with nuclear weapons at sea in effect. This forces Soviet naval air power as the Americans have no corresponding weapon to use against them, and nuclear bombardment of Kola itself would all but guarantee a response against a significant American or British strategic target. To balance the increased firepower, allow the US player to take any two of the following cards: SAM Trap, Special Forces, Fighter Recovery, Economic Control, Radar Decoys.

alterations.title: #2 Cruise Missiles
alterations.description: Play the scenario in 1985, allowing the US to use cruise missiles and adding US-6 to the US forces. The Soviet player may place an additional RORSAT in any zone of the map.

alterations.title: #3 All the Toys
alterations.description: Add 2 Ticonderoga VLS to the US forces, and add a Bear-G at Kola to the Soviet setup. The Victor-III (I) and the Akula may be placed anywhere in a North Sea Zone (placed last, after everything else is on the map).

scenarios.title: Baltic Bust-Up
scenarios.briefing: The Soviet Baltic Fleet attempts to break out into the North Sea. NATO must contain Soviet fast attack units before they spill out of the Skagerrak.
scenarios.victoryConditions: NATO wins by preventing Soviet breakout. Soviet wins by getting fast attack units past the Danish Strait and inflicting losses on NATO shipping in the North Sea.
scenarios.specialRules: Baltic-specific rules apply (see §7.4 and §8.4.2). The Danish Strait mining level and Norwegian status follow scenario start conditions.

scenarios.title: Campaign Game
scenarios.briefing:
The full war at sea. The campaign is built around a chosen **Start Type** (Strategic Surprise, Tactical Surprise, or Extended Build-up) and a chosen **Era** (1983, 1985, or 1989). The Era determines which units are on the board; the Start Type determines how the war begins — how prepared each side is, how many forces are pre-positioned, and what special rules apply.

*Recommended for first play: 1983 + Tactical Surprise, no options.*
scenarios.victoryConditions: Standard campaign victory conditions apply per (3.5): the Soviets must accumulate **four Hammer & Sickle markers** on locations overrun by their forces on the War and Invasion Tracks. NATO must slow or stop these advances by keeping convoys flowing, striking Soviet troop markers (7.5.5), and defending the Invasion Tracks (Norway and Denmark). See also (3.5.1) for NATO Losses tracking.

startTypes.label: Strategic Surprise
startTypes.description: Pre-war NATO is caught flat-footed. Convoys are forming up under-strength and the bulk of NATO's pre-positioning hasn't happened. Smaller pre-game force placements; harsher convoy penalties early.
startTypes.specialRules: All Convoys begin with two hits during setup and Turns 1 and 2. During Turns 3 through 5 this is reduced to one hit. From Turn 6, Convoys form normally with no hits. *Represents the lack of pre-war time to properly form-up NATO shipping; convoys have fewer ships for the first two weeks of the war.*

startTypes.label: Tactical Surprise (Standard)
startTypes.description: The 'standard' campaign baseline. NATO has had some warning and has begun mobilization, but is not at war footing. Designer-recommended for first plays.
startTypes.specialRules: No special rules. This is the baseline against which the other two start types are scaled.

startTypes.label: Extended Build-up
startTypes.description: Both sides have had weeks of warning and have fully mobilized. NATO has formed up the merchant navies of Europe; the Soviets are more prepared to use reserves or nuclear weapons. Largest pre-game force placements; Soviet First Strike Points start on the board.
startTypes.specialRules: The Soviet player takes 2 First Strike Points at the start of the game. NATO places two Convoys on Turns 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 (all odd Convoy turns). If NATO is unlucky with weather and there are not enough Convoys to place, missing Convoys are received as soon as they are available. *NATO has a huge number of convoy ships available; the Soviets have significant force at-sea.*

startTypeScaling.label: Breakdown choice — NATO may place 1 US Sturgeon and/or 1 US Los Angeles sub into the Destroyed box to take the matching breakdown counters, placed where the sub(s) were or with any at-sea Task Force lacking a submarine. Similarly NATO may place US 4-6 surface ships into the Destroyed box (replace each removed unit with one or two replacement ships). Any not placed may begin in the USA.
Ship units relocated to other NATO bases or at-sea TFs
One NATO Task Force may be formed up and placed within 2 Sea Zones of its origin port, including forces from that port. UK and FR ports count as the same origin port for this purpose.
Submarine Units placed anywhere on the map
Air Units placed On Patrol within range (MP or fighters)
The at-sea carriers beginning in TF Hammer may be relocated to new or existing Task Forces anywhere except the Mediterranean and not north of the GIUK Gap.
Optional: Draw 2 'options' markers from a cup and select one to keep. Repeat for each First Strike Point given to the Soviet player (maximum 2 picks).
The Soviet player may purchase Soviet Technology markers. Reduce the Spies Track by the number on each marker put into play.

The Soviet player may take one Tu-22 from the destroyed box (if present) by removing 2 Tu-16 Badgers or the Tu-95 Bear-G. Place it at Kola, Baltic, Black Sea, or Syrian bases (trading assets with the Far East).
Move up to three strike Air Units to any Soviet bases (except Cuba).
Move up to three Surface Units to any Soviet bases (except Cuba).
Subs placed anywhere on the map
Additional subs within 2 zones of a Soviet base (except Cuba)
Soviet Task Forces created pre-game from units of a single Soviet port; placed on the map anywhere marked with a Poor detection (Good if within 1 zone of a NATO TF)
Roll weather for all zones. If weather is placed in a zone with a Task Force, place a 'Moved' marker on it (the Task Force has been within the Bad Weather for some time).
Battletales: roll detection on all NATO Task Forces at sea (1 die each). Soviet may select one TF (two for Extended Build-up) and use two dice instead
Begin the game starting with the Convoy Placement Phase.
Optional: Draw 2 'options' markers from a cup and select one to keep. Repeat for each First Strike Point discarded or spy expended (maximum 2 picks).

yearVariants.notes: Base era. Use the printed setup for the chosen Start Type as published.
Adds NATO cruise-missile capability. Both sides receive 1985 unit additions and one or two unit replacements (force modernization).

Adds further unit modernizations on both sides (Ticonderoga VLS, additional SSNs for NATO; Tu-22 Backfire and Kuznetsov for the Soviets). Apply BOTH the 1985 additions AND the 1989 additions on top of the 1983 base.

scenarios.specialRules: Common setup procedure (10-step NATO then 10-step Soviet pre-game choices) appears at the front of the campaign rules. Both players draw 5 cards each. Choose Start Type before anything else; all other scaled values follow from that choice. Begin the game starting with the Convoy Placement Phase.
